_doc: DNS64/NAT64/CLAT data for reaching IPv4-only sites (github.com etc.) on an IPv6-only WiFi network. Consumed by configuration_network.nix (services.resolved.extraConfig + fallbackDns) — edit the JSON, not the .nix. Companion to wireguard-endpoints.json/wireguard-public-endpoints.json's dual-stack fields; this file is the NAT64-specific counterpart. See also a0_tasks/PLAN_ipv6-only-wifi.md history.
_public_dns64_fallback_resolvers_doc: nat64.net's public DNS64 resolvers (Kasper Dupont, Tayga) — moved here from the old inline extraConfig literals in configuration_network.nix per repo principle 6 (no hardcoded IPs in .nix source). They synthesize 64:ff9b::/96-style AAAA records for v4-only names, reachable over plain IPv6. Escape hatch for an IPv6-only WiFi with no NAT64 gateway of its own and no WG tunnel yet: dnscrypt-proxy2 (127.0.0.1, first in the DNS= list) fails over to these when its DoH upstreams are unreachable over v4. UNTESTED end-to-end outside the nixosTest in test-ipv6-only.nix — verify these are still current at https://nat64.net before relying on them in the field.
_v6_fallback_dns_doc: services.resolved.fallbackDns, IPv6-capable versions. The previous value ([1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9]) is v4-only and useless on a v6-only network — resolved could never even reach those IPs to ask them anything. 2606:4700:4700::1111 = Cloudflare's well-known IPv6 anycast resolver (mirrors 1.1.1.1); 2620:fe::fe = Quad9's well-known IPv6 anycast resolver (mirrors 9.9.9.9), filtered/malware-blocking, DNSSEC-validating. Both are long-standing, well-known addresses (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 launched 2018-04; Quad9 published fe::fe alongside its v4 anycast at general availability) and are the standard v6 fallback pairing cited alongside their respective v4 addresses in public documentation. resolved's fallbackDns only fires when the DNS= list is completely empty, so this is a last-resort safety net, not the primary DNS64 path (see public_dns64_fallback_resolvers above for that).
_nat64_wellknown_prefix_doc: RFC 6052 well-known NAT64 prefix. Tier 1 of the CLAT ladder in configuration_network.nix's clat-on-v6only dispatcher, and preferred over ANY third party: many v6-only networks run NAT64 here while publishing no DNS64 at all, and forcing this prefix keeps every IPv4 packet on the local gateway. Was hardcoded in the .nix (principle 6: no literal IPs in Nix source).
_nat64_probe_target_doc: 8.8.8.8 expressed behind nat64_wellknown_prefix. One bounded ping6 to this proves a local NAT64 exists before any other tier is considered. Was hardcoded in the .nix.
_clat_plat_prefix_doc: TIER 3a — the fleet's OWN NAT64 prefix, once one exists. null = not deployed yet. When set, clatd is forced to this prefix and never queries anyone else. This is the intended permanent answer to 'IPv6-only WiFi with no NAT64': self-hosted, no volunteer service in the path. NOTE the cheaper route that may make this permanently unnecessary — wireguard-endpoints.json already supports tunnel_mode=full (0.0.0.0/0 into the tunnel). Once a wg hub has a public IPv6 endpoint the tunnel establishes on a v6-only network and carries IPv4 itself, encrypted, with no NAT64 anywhere. See a0_tasks/PLAN_ipv6-only-wifi.md.
_clat_dns64_direct_doc: TIER 3b — LAST RESORT, PRIVACY-RELEVANT, DELIBERATELY OFF. When true and every earlier tier has failed, public_dns64_fallback_resolvers are handed to clatd as `dns64-servers=`, which makes clatd query them DIRECTLY via its own Net::DNS resolver (clatd 1.6 source, sub get_plat_prefix) — bypassing systemd-resolved, dnscrypt-proxy2 and per-link DNS entirely. That bypass is the whole point: on 2026-08-12 clatd died with 'No PLAT prefix could be discovered' because its RFC7050 query went to dnscrypt-proxy2 on 127.0.0.1, whose upstreams are IPv4 literals and therefore unreachable on a v6-only link, so it TIMED OUT rather than failing over. The cost of enabling this: clatd adopts nat64.net's prefix, so ALL plain IPv4 traffic is translated by a volunteer service and visible to it in v4 form (WireGuard's own crypto still protects the tunnels; nothing else). Left false so the machine FAILS CLOSED with no IPv4 rather than silently transiting a third party. Flip to true only as a conscious, temporary choice — it logs a daemon.warning naming the cost every time it engages.
_clat_enable_doc: Enables 464XLAT (CLAT) via services.clatd or the hand-rolled systemd unit (see configuration_network.nix). DNS64 alone only helps hostnames that get resolved through the synthesizing resolver; anything that skips DNS and connects to a raw IPv4 literal (e.g. wireguard-endpoints.json hub.host = 35.226.147.64) has nothing to translate its packets. clatd self-discovers the NAT64 prefix via RFC7050 (ipv4only.arpa) and no-ops when native IPv4 already exists, so it is safe to leave enabled unconditionally on a dual-stack-capable laptop — it does nothing until the uplink is genuinely v6-only.
